content: Tecovirimat, a weak inducer of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, can reduce the levels or effects of various medications by altering their metabolism. Similarly, tecovirimat may increase the levels or effects of certain drugs metabolized by CYP2C19, such as treprostinil, tretinoin, trimipramine, velpatasvir, voriconazole, voxilaprevir, ambrisentan, amiodarone, apalutamide, citalopram, clobazam, clomipramine, and carisoprodol. This occurs due to its weak inhibitory effect on CYP2C19 and CYP2C8 enzymes. In these cases, monitoring for adverse effects is recommended. Additionally, tecovirimat can decrease the levels or effects of other drugs, including abemaciclib, abiraterone, acalabrutinib, ado-trastuzumab emtansine, alfentanil, alfuzosin, alprazolam, atazanavir, atogepant, atorvastatin, avanafil, axitinib, bedaquiline, benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen, benzphetamine, bosentan, bosutinib, brentuximab vedotin, brexpiprazole, brigatinib, bromocriptine, budesonide, buprenorphine (in various formulations), buspirone, busulfan, cabozantinib, calcifediol, calcitriol, carbamazepine, cariprazine, ceritinib, chlordiazepoxide, chloroquine, chlorpheniramine, cilostazol, clarithromycin, and clonazepam. This reduction in drug levels is due to its effect on CYP3A4 metabolism. For these medications, close monitoring of their effectiveness is essential. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and caution is advised. In all cases, healthcare providers should carefully monitor patients for changes in drug effectiveness or adverse effects when tecovirimat is co-administered with these medications.
